asetek-forte-direct-drive-wheelbase: Solid quick release and easy software; a few random shutoffs.
asetek-invicta-direct-drive-wheelbase: An upgrade from Fanatec or MOZA for many; firmware issues for some.
asetek-la-prima-direct-drive-wheelbase: Smooth, with no cogging; a couple had software or power issues.
fanatec-clubsport-dd-plus: A clear step up from the CSL DD; firmware and driver trouble.
fanatec-csl-cockpit-v1-5: Surprisingly rigid for a budget rig; the low seat is uncomfortable.
fanatec-csl-dd-8-nm: A big jump from Logitech or Thrustmaster; the quick release has play.
fanatec-csl-elite-pedals-v2: A good upgrade from G29 pedals; the brake is firm or fiddly.
gt-omega-prime: No flex even with strong bases; some reworked the pedal plate.
heusinkveld-handbrake: Compact and good for rallycross; stubby and pricey for one.
heusinkveld-sprint: Much more consistent braking; many swap the elastomer for springs.
heusinkveld-ultimate-plus: Durable with good brake modulation; the firm default takes time.
logitech-pro-racing-pedals: A big upgrade over G29 pedals; the throttle throw is long.
logitech-pro-racing-wheel: Plug-and-play direct drive; the rim choice is thin.
logitech-rs-h-shifter: Premium, with a firm throw; the stiff springs are hard work.
logitech-rs-pedals: A big upgrade over G29 pedals; the brake is stiff or soggy.
logitech-rs-round-wheel: Grippy leather and rubber; it feels small for rally.
logitech-rs-shifter-handbrake: Smooth handbrake and firm click; less mechanical for a couple.
logitech-rs-track-wheel: Comfortable GT-style rim with good grip; slippery for a couple.
logitech-rs50: A big upgrade from a G29 or G923; some disconnects or failures.
moza-gs-v2p: Aluminium build and good buttons, with no creaking or rattling.
moza-hbp-handbrake: Sturdy and adjustable; updates broke it for some.
moza-ks-pro: Quiet with good buttons; the grip shape hurts some hands.
moza-mbooster-active-pedal: Realistic, precise braking once tuned; big and slow to dial in.
moza-r3: A smooth step up from Logitech; some outgrow it within a year.
moza-r5: Strong value, but the bundled pedals are weak.
next-level-racing-gtlite-pro: Comfortable, adjustable seat; folding is a hassle.
next-level-racing-gtracer-2-0: Rigid, easy starter cockpit; some pedals are hard to fit.
next-level-racing-wheel-stand-2-0: Very rigid with strong bases; heavy to fold and move.
next-level-racing-wheel-stand-lite-2-0: Rolls out and stores easily; flexes with stronger bases.
playseat-trophy: Comfortable and easy to move; the pedal tray flexes with load cells.
sim-lab-gt1-evo: Very rigid for the price; the shifter arm wobbles.
sim-lab-p1x-pro: A big step up from tube rigs; the angled uprights annoy.
sim-lab-p1x-ultimate: Straight uprights give lots of mounting options; some sloppy QC.
sim-lab-xp1: Adjustable with smooth braking; notchy or squeaky until greased.
simagic-alpha-evo: Enough torque for most owners; less of a leap than hyped for a few.
simagic-alpha-evo-pro: Good software, though a minority find the feel robotic.
simagic-alpha-evo-sport: Beats Moza and belt bases; some run out of torque.
simagic-alpha-ultimate: More torque than most need for the money; software lacks for a few.
simagic-ds-8x: Solid H-pattern and sequential in one; a few levers failed.
simagic-gt-neo: Great value with plenty of controls; the rubber grips are hard.
simagic-p1000: Modular and adjustable; the brake elastomers drift.
simagic-p2000: Controllable hydraulic trail braking; leaks after a year for some.
simagic-tb-rs: A smooth hydraulic handbrake; a couple dislike the foam grip.
simucube-2-pro: Many expect it to be their last base; filtered or noisy to a few.
simucube-3-pro: A clear step up from Fanatec; little gain over an SC2 Pro for some.
simucube-activepedal-pro: Refined brake feel and good software; close to MOZA's mBooster.
thrustmaster-ferrari-488-gt3-wheel-add-o: Good feel and buttons; LEDs fail on other bases.
thrustmaster-th8a: Reliable for years; it lacks a mechanical feel.
simagic-alpha-mini: Solid and strong, a big step up from Logitech; fiddly software.
thrustmaster-t-lcm: Good-value brake upgrade; the stock springs are weak.
fanatec-clubsport-pedals-v3: A big step up from entry pedals; toy-like after Heusinkveld.
fanatec-gran-turismo-dd-pro: Satisfying first direct drive over a G29; numb next to others.
thrustmaster-t818: Strong, quiet, detailed feedback; power supplies fail.
fanatec-clubsport-dd: A big jump from a CSL DD; a couple had early failure and poor service.
simagic-alpha: Smooth, quiet 15 Nm that beats Moza and Fanatec; a noise for one.
moza-r12-v2: Useful software with SimHub support; some heard clicking.
simagic-p1000i: Inverted pedals kind to sore knees; the brake is hard to dial in.
gt-omega-prime-lite: Sturdy with no flex; several got untapped parts.
thrustmaster-t150: Budget first wheel with real force feedback; durability is weak.
gt-omega-titan: Sturdy, narrow and easy to move; some flex at the shifter or deck.
simagic-fx-pro: Sturdy, feature-rich GT or formula wheel; it creaks.
simucube-2-sport: Fast, detailed response for catching slides; some noise or heat.
next-level-racing-f-gt-lite: Rigid and easy to set up; flexes under heavy braking.
thrustmaster-t300rs: Long-lived, with feedback some prefer to Logitech; can run hot.
thrustmaster-t-gt-ii: Better road feel than a T300; base vibration takes getting used to.
moza-r9-v3: Far more responsive than Logitech wheels; a marginal step for some.
simagic-p500: Plug-in load cell upgrade from G29; brake consistency is a doubt.
fanatec-clubsport-gt-cockpit: Rigid and very adjustable; knees can hit the base mount.
sim-lab-gt1-pro: Solid and quick to build; a few had loose uprights.
thrustmaster-ferrari-f1-wheel-add-on: Many buttons and rotaries; the plastic feels cheap.
gt-omega-prime-lite-r: Good value and solid up to about 12 Nm; the pedal plate is weak.
